diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of Corollary \ref{cor:LS} comes directly by combining Theorem~\ref{th:main_ls} with Theorem~\ref{thm:mainthm}

issues.failure_explanation: The L^2 error of the least-squares surrogate is homogeneous of degree one in the target: scaling the initial condition u_0 (equivalently replacing f by alpha*f) scales the error by |alpha| while leaving the best s-term support S unchanged, but the stated right-hand side C(rho,p)(m/log(m/epsilon))^{1/2-1/p} + 2||n||_inf is independent of f. Hence for large |alpha| the inequality fails, so th:main_ls (and cor:LS, which copies the same bound) is false as written. The paper's own best s-term bound (eq:bounderror) and the compressed-sensing bound (cor:CS, and the display in sec:holomorphic) both carry the factor ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)}, and the appendix invokes thm:mainthm — whose only quantitative content is the bound B(u_0,T,M) on ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)} — confirming the factor was dropped.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the factor ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)} in th:main_ls and ||f_v||_{L^inf(E_rho)} (bounded by B(u_0,T,M) via thm:mainthm) in cor:LS; rates, sample complexity, and scope are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantees of th:main_ls and cor:LS are false as stated. The advertised quasi-optimal least-squares rate (best m-term rate up to log factors, contribution 2 of the introduction) survives once the factor is restored, so no headline claim is lost.
issues.title: Least-squares error bound omits the factor ||f||_{L^inf(E_rho)}; bound is scale-invariant false
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single inserted factor already present in the paper's own eq:bounderror and cor:CS; every substantive claim (rate, log factors, curse-of-dimensionality statement) survives, with no new lemma or argument needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The bound in th:main_ls (copied verbatim in cor:LS) contains p in C(rho,p) and in the exponent 1/2-1/p, yet the statement quantifies over neither p nor any range containing it, so the guarantee is ill-formed as written: the reader cannot tell for which p it holds, and the rate decays in m only when p<2 (for p>=2 the exponent is nonnegative). This is a statement defect, not a proof mismatch, dependency failure, or inference error; the intended range must be supplied (e.g., 0<p<2 or the range from the cited LS theorem). The contrast with cor:CS ('for every 0 < p <= 1') and eq:bounderror ('for all 0<p<=q<=infty') shows the quantifier was dropped, and unlike those, no in-source range forces a unique repair.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit quantifier over p (e.g., 'for every 0<p<2', or the range intended from the cited Theorem 6.1) to th:main_ls and cor:LS.
issues.overall_effect: th:main_ls and cor:LS are not well-formed guarantees until the range of p is declared; adding any standard quantifier restores the statements with no loss of content.
issues.title: Parameter p in the least-squares error bound is never quantified
issues.why_classification: A one-line statement repair (insert the quantifier) with no change to the argument, rate, or advertised scope; minor.
